a4717.speech: Said the initiative has two main objectives: on the one hand to present the opportunities for on-site processing of agricultural products offered by the Gdiz and the impact on job creation and the transformation of the Beninese economy, and on the other hand to recall the basis of the measures to preserve raw materials and the advantages for local and national economic development. "Everything that concerns the agricultural world is of interest to the chamber of agriculture. Faced with this confirmed will of the government, we thought it right that the producers should see what is happening," he said. ; Found the visit timely in allowing them to see the reality for themselves and to understand why expatriates come to buy Beninese cotton, cashew, soya and other raw materials: "Today, we know what they do with it and why they do it." ; Said it is also an occasion for them to know how much they are valued and how they participate in the country's development through their production, which is now processed and given value at this site: "No one will come and develop our country in our place; it is ourselves, and it is only through such acts that we can do it."

a4717.speaker: Aidath Mare, head of an NGO supporting women's cooperatives in the processing of soya and shea in the north
a4717.speech: Very moved by what she saw: "That it should be Benin that today manufactures threads, towels, the uniforms of our police officers, customs officers and soldiers which we used to buy abroad, that is wonderful, we are really happy." ; Called on actors in the agricultural world to redouble their efforts in the production of cotton, soya, cashew: "It is a notable advance that must be saluted and it will transform our country," while thanking the government for the initiative of setting up the Gdiz.

a4717.speaker: Ali Deladi, president of the rice producers of the commune of Karimama
a4717.speech: Promised to sensitise farmers to increasing production: "We must serve our country before thinking of exporting. It is a feat that we today process cashew, soya and cotton at home."

a4717.speaker: Oumarou Medawa, first deputy mayor of the commune of Karimama
a4717.speech: Considered, in view of what the participants saw on site, that it is important that the Beninese understand that Benin is truly committed to industrial transformation: "We visited the various processing plants and one can easily notice that the cotton, cashew and soya that we produce in Benin are processed in this centre. We will have to understand that this is a centre which, apart from processing, creates employment. That is to be saluted." ; Said it was important to come and see, because many do not really know what is happening at the Glo-Djigbe industrial zone.

a4717.speaker: Letondji Beheton, Managing Director of Sipi Benin S.a.
a4717.speech: Explained from beginning to end the processing that has been taking place in this business centre for 16 months, saying that the structural transformation desired for a new Benin means the industrialisation of the economy, to move it from an economy based on the export of raw materials to an economy where these raw materials are henceforth processed for more added value, more wealth and to create more jobs: "One cannot develop a country on the basis of foreign aid. What is needed instead is the mobilisation of resources, while having a strong economy. And a strong economy for Benin is an economy that will henceforth be based on the processing of our agricultural products." ; Continued that all the factories installed in the zone use exclusively Beninese raw materials: "It is fitting that producers realise what becomes of their raw materials. The transformation is real here. This zone is a representation of our country with all the languages that are spoken there."

a4909.speaker: Ministry of Finance – Republic of Ghana (report distributed by the APO Group)
a4909.speech: According to the report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the Ministry of Finance – Republic of Ghana, the approval of these reforms is not just a policy shift—it is a decisive step toward a stronger, more prosperous Ghana.

a4924.speaker: Community source (anonymous)
a4924.speech: Told Daily Trust that the victim was rushed to a nearby hospital but was denied treatment due to procedural restrictions surrounding gunshot wounds, and that he eventually died from excessive blood loss.

a4924.speaker: Musa Muhammad, DSP, Bayelsa State Police Public Relations Officer
a4924.speech: Confirming the recent killing, said investigations are underway to apprehend the perpetrators.

a4924.speaker: Salisu Shehu Umar, Dr., Rector of Auchi Polytechnic
a4924.speech: Stated in an interview that the management has expelled over 58 students for cult-related offences between 2022 and 2025, emphasising the school's zero-tolerance policy toward cultism: “Cultism is a serious problem in this part of the country. We have expelled over 58 students since 2022, and we're not relenting.”

a4924.speaker: Monday Okpebholo, Senator, Edo State Governor
a4924.speech: Has vowed to eradicate cultism, describing cultists as “enemies of the state”; while addressing youths during a peaceful rally at the Government House, reaffirmed his administration's commitment to protecting the lives of all Edo citizens: “These cultists are our enemies and want to kill the dreams of the state. But they will not stop us. We will do all that is necessary to ensure cultism becomes a thing of the past.”

a5449.speaker: Eric Seddy Kutortse, Executive Chairman of First Sky Group
a5449.speech: Has called on local professionals to spearhead the future of Ghana's energy sector. He emphasized that the country possesses the necessary local expertise to manage both current and upcoming energy projects, which are crucial for economic growth ; during a recent inspection of a 50MW solar photovoltaic power station under construction in Yendi, highlighted the importance of utilizing Ghana's natural resources—such as sun, wind, and water—to ensure energy security and decrease dependence on imports ; noted that this landmark project not only signifies a major investment, but also positions Ghana as a leader in the global shift towards renewable energy, and stated that all experts involved in the project are Ghanaians.

a5449.speaker: Samuel Kofi Dzamesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority
a5449.speech: Praised First Sky Group for this significant achievement, marking it as the first solar plant built by a Ghanaian company, in contrast to previous projects typically undertaken by foreign entities. He explained that First Sky is responsible for the engineering, procurement, and financing of the initiative, which will provide power for sale while repaying the financing over eight years.

a5449.speaker: Owuraku Aidoo, Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Energy
a5449.speech: Confirmed that the Yendi project aligns with the government's goal of achieving 10% of its energy mix from renewable sources.

a5449.speaker: Emmanuel Adumua-Bossman, Deputy Chief of Staff
a5449.speech: Expressed satisfaction with the project's progress, highlighting the warranty on the solar panels, ensuring their performance over the next twenty-five years.

a5449.speaker: Kwesi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, Board Chair of Bui Power Authority
a5449.speech: Also commended First Sky's accomplishments, asserting that it reflects the potential of indigenous companies to contribute significantly to the nation's development.

a5561.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, ACT-Wazalendo presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Pledged to conduct a peaceful and issue-based campaign; said they would conduct peaceful campaigns and called upon all people in Zanzibar to support them in safeguarding peace and stability ; "Our position remains clear, we continue to reject early voting, but we will not boycott the election."

a5561.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, ACT-Wazalendo presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Pledged to centre his campaign on issues affecting ordinary Zanzibaris, particularly the preservation of historical sites and cultural heritage, which he says the current administration has neglected ; thanked supporters for their continued loyalty and urged them to deliver victory for ACT-Wazalendo, promising better governance and inclusive leadership.

a5561.speaker: Juma Ali Khatib, ADATADEA presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Endorsed CCM candidate Dr Hussein Mwinyi, citing the incumbent's 'strong performance' over the past five years: "Dr Mwinyi has demonstrated leadership, and I believe supporting his re-election is in the best interest of Zanzibar."

a5561.speaker: Naima Salum Hamad, UDP presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Advocates for the rights of women, children and people with special needs.

a5561.speaker: Ameir Hassan Ameir, DemokrasiaMakini presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Has pledged a monthly allowance of 500,000/- to every Zanzibari if elected.

a5561.speaker: Hamad Ibrahim Mohammed, UPDP presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Promised constitutional reforms, a chief ministerial system and the construction of nuclear power plants on Unguja and Pemba.

a5561.speaker: Hamad Rashid Mohammed, ADC presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Said his party prioritises food self-sufficiency, value addition to export crops like cloves and seaweed and public asset declarations for government officials.

a5561.speaker: Shafii Hassan Suleiman, DP presidential candidate
a5561.speech: Said the party focuses on peace, job creation through industrial development and supports early voting to accommodate citizens with unavoidable obligations on election day.

a5561.speaker: Justice George Joseph Kazi, ZEC Chairman
a5561.speech: Confirmed that nomination forms have been issued to 17 registered political parties, as per Section 46 of the Zanzibar Elections Act No. 4 of 2018 ; "This process promotes transparency, accountability and integrity in the electoral process," adding that nomination day is set for September 11, with campaigns officially beginning at 4:01 p.m. the same day ; urged all aspirants to fill out the forms carefully and assured them of technical support from ZEC if needed.

a5694.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5694.speech: Announced a series of bold initiatives aimed at reducing unemployment in Lesotho, with a particular focus on creating opportunities for young people; said during a media briefing this week that by encouraging civil servants aged 50 and above to take early retirement, the government could create more space for young people to enter the workforce: “The government will also explore ways to reduce taxes, making it easier for businesses to hire more youths.”

a5694.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5694.speech: Instructed ministries that are able to do so to allocate two percent of their annual budgets to the Youth Development Fund: “This contribution will help us combat unemployment by directly supporting youth initiatives.”

a5694.speaker: Bureau of Statistics / Lesotho Labour Force Survey 2024
a5694.speech: Cited by the Prime Minister as showing that 50 percent of the population is currently unemployed, with youths making up less than half of this number.

a5694.speaker: Dr Retšelisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a5694.speech: Said in February this year during her 2025-2025 budget speech in parliament that 38.9 percent of youth in Lesotho were unemployed, with young women bearing the brunt at 41 percent.

a5694.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5694.speech: Pointed to international factors, including U.S. executive orders and the withdrawal of Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) aid, as having worsened the unemployment situation.

a5694.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5694.speech: Said the government aimed to “significantly reduce unemployment and provide more opportunities for Lesotho's youth”, and emphasized his personal commitment to ensuring the success of his plans, stating he “will spend time each week visiting projects to monitor progress”.

a5993.speaker: Dr. Chukwuemeka Amuta, Abia State Team Lead of Caritas Nigeria
a5993.speech: In his opening remarks, underscored the urgent need to translate policies into tangible actions; speaking on the theme “Moving from Policy to Action: Advancing Gender Justice and Child Protection through Multi-Sectoral Response”, emphasised the significance of the dialogue as a platform for fostering consensus among stakeholders and urged participants to focus on identifying practical strategies to strengthen existing policies and laws addressing gender justice and child protection.

a5993.speaker: Dr. Charles Ukauwa, public health expert (keynote speaker)
a5993.speech: Delved into the pressing issues of gender-based violence and child abuse in Abia State; highlighted the critical challenges faced in combating these societal ills, offering an overview of existing legal frameworks and support systems including the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act (VAPP Act), the Female Persons Right of Inheritance Law, and the roles played by the NSCDC, NAPTIP, the judiciary and civil society organisations, noting these underscore the importance of a collective approach; noted that despite commendable efforts, significant gaps persist in the enforcement and coordination of responses to gender-based violence (GBV) and stressed the urgent need for reforms to strengthen legal and institutional frameworks; called for the establishment of forensic centers to enhance evidence management, the creation of specialized courts to expedite GBV cases, and the development of effective referral centers for prompt intervention; emphasised the need to address cultural norms through comprehensive legal, policy, and behavioral change initiatives, while advocating for a redefinition of the Ministry of Women Affairs; and highlighted the pivotal role of families, religious and traditional institutions, as well as the hospitality industry, in advancing gender justice and supporting child protection efforts.

a5993.speaker: Barr. Akudo Amanamba, President of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) Abia State Chapter
a5993.speech: In her submission, expressed concern over the reluctance of survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) to pursue justice, attributing this hesitancy to the fear of stigma and the absence of adequate support systems to assist survivors in their quest for justice.

a5993.speaker: Mr. Richard Okoro, Executive Director of Rural Development Planners (RUDEP)
a5993.speech: Criticized the government for its lack of commitment to tackling GBV and child protection issues; highlighted the absence of emergency shelters for survivors as a glaring gap, emphasizing the need for measurable actions to address these pressing challenges.

a5993.speaker: Stakeholders and participants at the Multi-Stakeholders Dialogue (panel discussions)
a5993.speech: Underscored the importance of establishing a functional and well-coordinated state response to tackle gender-based violence and safeguard children’s rights; stressed the urgency of implementing existing laws, including the VAPP Act and the Female Inheritance Law, the importance of creating safe spaces for survivors and enhancing the quality of public education as a preventive measure; highlighted the need to empower women and girls through education and economic opportunities, while actively engaging religious and traditional leaders to challenge harmful cultural norms; and emphasised that survivors of GBV must remain at the forefront of all response mechanisms.

a5995.speaker: Ministers of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
a5995.speech: Warned about the insufficiency of funding in the face of rising humanitarian needs, and are seeking to establish sustainable mechanisms and strengthen regional coordination in order to better protect populations.

a5995.speaker: Mahamadou Kassogue, Malian Justice Minister (representing the Prime Minister)
a5995.speech: Stressed at the opening ceremony that only 50% of people in humanitarian need in Mali were able to be assisted in 2024, for lack of sufficient funding, a similar figure being observed in Burkina Faso and Niger.

a5995.speaker: Mali 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP)
a5995.speech: According to the plan, 6.5 million people were in need, with an initial budget of USD 771.3 million to target 4.7 million; but because of the cuts the plan was scaled back to 2.1 million beneficiaries and USD 223.3 million.

a5995.speaker: Ghassum Diagne, representing the humanitarian partners
a5995.speech: Recalled the importance of placing the protection of populations - particularly women and children - at the heart of interventions, stressing that current funding remains notoriously insufficient to guarantee effective responses.

a6070.speaker: Mohamed Shire, Director-General of the Ministry of Planning, Investment and Economic Development of Somalia
a6070.speech: Outlined Somalia's National Transformation Plan (NTP 2025-2029) and Vision 2060 as the country's guiding frameworks for sustainable development ; shared examples of how the Somali Aid Architecture enhances coordination among government institutions, international partners, and communities to deliver tangible results ; stressed the importance of country-led, evidence-based, and effective partnerships to achieve sustainable progress despite shrinking aid flows ; emphasized the need for strong alignment between global partnerships and Somalia's long-term priorities to ensure effective cooperation and lasting impact.

a6130.speaker: Ya-Na Abukari II, Overlord of Dagbon
a6130.speech: Has entreated the government to expedite action on the perennial water crisis affecting residents of Tamale and Yendi in the Northern Region ; said the persistent water crisis was affecting livelihoods, businesses and the overall well-being of the people; hence, urgent intervention was needed to bring relief to the people ; said that the construction of the Tamale and Yendi water projects was the surest way of resolving the situation, adding “when the water projects in these two major cities are completed, it will facilitate distribution and access, and the sufferings of the people will reduce”.

a6130.speaker: Ya-Na Abukari II, Overlord of Dagbon
a6130.speech: Reiterated his commitment to collaborate with the government and other stakeholders to drive development in the area, particularly the water sector ; said there were many opportunities for business growth in those areas but due to the lack of a reliable water supply system, investments were being thwarted.

a6130.speaker: Ya-Na Abukari II, Overlord of Dagbon
a6130.speech: Commended the chiefs and people for their resilience over the years, and for ensuring sustainable peace and harmony for accelerated development.

a6130.speaker: Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources
a6130.speech: Said efforts were being made to address the perennial water crisis in the two cities ; said the President had held extensive discussions with the ministry to come up with a comprehensive strategy to tackle the issue ; “Our team who include engineers, will be on the ground to assess the situation and ensure that once the project commences, it proceeds efficiently, unlike previous efforts,” he assured ; said all relevant stakeholders would be engaged to help implement sustainable and long-term solutions to the water crisis.

a6130.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana
a6130.speech: During his recent “Thank You Tour” in Yendi, assured the Ya-Na that the government would source funding to fix the water challenges in the two cities ; said efforts would be made to source water from the White Volta in Yapei to serve the southern parts of Tamale, while obsolete machines at the Dalung Pumping station in the Kumbungu District would be replaced to increase supplies to other parts of the metropolis.

a6220.speaker: Asset declarations of Senators Dillion and Sogbie submitted to the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission (2024)
a6220.speech: Reveal that each Senator receives a substantial annual gross salary of $129,992, translating to about $10,832 monthly.

a6220.speaker: 2024 salary structure document for the House of Representatives
a6220.speech: Indicates that each representative earns a gross annual salary of $105,000, or approximately $8,810 monthly, in addition to a gas allowance of $26,700 annually.

a6220.speaker: Approved 2025 national budget of Liberia (document)
a6220.speech: Outlines projected revenue of approximately US$861.8 million and total expenditures of US$880.6 million, resulting in a projected deficit of around US$18.8 million; allocates $44.3 million to the National Legislature, US$1.5 million to the Office of the Speaker (gross annual salary of $245,540), US$1.2 million to the Deputy Speaker (gross annual salary of $208,940) and US$1.2 million to the Office of the Pro Tempore (gross annual salary of $256,203).

a6360.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC
a6360.speech: “CPHIA constitutes an essential step in the efforts made by African countries and Africa CDC to build strong and self-reliant health systems,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC. ; “It offers a strategic platform where leaders, public health experts and communities can rethink and transform health financing, so that the continent’s health security is driven by African leadership, innovation and partnerships,” he said.

a6360.speaker: Africa CDC (press release distributed by APO Group)
a6360.speech: According to the press release distributed by APO Group on behalf of Africa CDC, the 2025 edition of the conference has a particular global significance. It will precede the meeting of G20 health ministers, scheduled under the South African presidency at the beginning of November 2025.

a6360.speaker: Professor Olive Shisana, co-chair of CPHIA 2025 and president of Evidence Based Solutions
a6360.speech: “CPHIA represents a decisive opportunity to promote an African agenda for health, founded on self-reliance and transformation,” explained Professor Olive Shisana, co-chair of the 2025 edition. She added: “We want to agree on a Durban Declaration that will place these priorities at the forefront of the G20 and Global Fund meetings scheduled for November.”

a6360.speaker: Dr Nhlanhla Msomi, president of AfricaBio
a6360.speech: “The BIO Africa Convention is proud to partner with Africa CDC to connect science, innovation and entrepreneurship to public health,” said Dr Nhlanhla Msomi, president of AfricaBio. And he added: “Together, we can mobilise Africa’s life sciences ecosystem to strengthen the continent’s health resilience and self-reliance.”

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: According to him, the project benefits over 10,000 people through electricity connections to two public health facilities, nine primary schools and four secondary schools, among others.

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: "The project has greatly improved the local economy of the area where businesses that create job opportunities are flourishing. We have also greatly improved the education and health for the area." ; "Before electricity, teachers and health personnel were not interested to work in the area which is very remote but today, many of them are interested to work in the area."

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: "One of the key elements in this project is the preservation of the mountain's already fragile ecosystem through reduction of deforestation and dependence on traditional energy sources." ; says the provision of a reliable source of energy to the mountain's surrounding communities for cooking and home lighting has contributed towards preventing people from depleting the trees from the mountain ; "So this is not just about providing electricity to the people but also creating a sustainable future for communities while protecting the natural beauty and biodiversity of our Mulanje Mountain."

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: Says climate change has sometimes made electricity generation difficult either due to low water levels brought by high temperatures or flooding which leads to blocking of water flow in penstocks because of increased debris. "Our project has a water shade management program through which various clubs concerned with tree planting were formed within the communities. These clubs get support in terms of seedlings from MMCT and Sukambizi Tea Association of Lujeri Tea Estate."

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: Says the agro-processing facility will be the main off-taker of Mega electricity and will in turn make the project more sustainable, and will provide market and incentives for the communities who will be supplying various fruits, thereby encouraging environmental sustainability. "The facility will encourage the communities to grow and take care of fruit trees and various forests products such as bees for honey."

a6372.speaker: Samuel Mambo, Mega operations manager
a6372.speech: "This will make our project much more sustainable as we aim to connect 10 000 households in Mulanje and sell the excess power to Escom."

a6372.speaker: Nande, Group Village Head
a6372.speech: Says the electricity project has also improved students' grades in class compared to the past as they are now able to study during long hours; further observes expectant mothers no longer travel for long distances to access improved health care due to electricity.

a6372.speaker: Linda Ndovi Jere, Usadf country programme coordinator
a6372.speech: Salutes Mega's focus on the long term environmental and economic advantages of the project, stating that using electricity for valuable intentions such as agro-processing exhibits Mega's forethought toward climate action and economic empowerment for the communities. "When Mega applied for the grant what fascinated us was the productive use of energy they proposed that the community around here want to embark on." ; "So this project will not only be about electricity but also improvement of the livelihoods of local communities."

a6372.speaker: Vera Phiri, Mzuzu-based youth environmental advocate
a6372.speech: Says expanding access to electricity in rural areas can help reduce deforestation in Malawi by reducing use of biomass for energy, as demand for wood fuel and charcoal will be reduced.

a6372.speaker: World Bank (17th Malawi Economic Monitor)
a6372.speech: Recently warned that the universal electricity access target by 2030 will remain an ambitious target if the country does not break away from the pattern of slow progress and financing and sector coordination; emphasised the need for expanding the grid and fast growth of the off-grid solar market to achieve universal access; and observed that the country needs about $3 billion (over K5 trillion) to meet targets for energy connections and demands prescribed in Malawi 2063.

a6471.speaker: General Michael Langley, Commander of the U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a6471.speech: “Our Secretary of State has always said the global environment has changed and things that we true years ago, have changed,” said at the conference on Tuesday. “The things we depended on for indicators and warnings have changed.”

a6471.speaker: General Michael Langley, Commander of the U.S. Africa Command (on partnering across Africa)
a6471.speech: Told Mmegi that despite the setback in West Africa, Africom was assessing other opportunities to engage with the continent: “We see a lot of different places to partner, across the African continent. We see that, we search it out. I travel with my USAID, and also my diplomatic adviser as well, engaging with presidents across coastal West Africa.”

a6471.speaker: General Michael Langley, Commander of the U.S. Africa Command (on Somalia)
a6471.speech: Said he was recently in Somalia engaging with President Hassan Sheikh Mohammed on the way ahead for Somalia: “(In Somalia) it’s not just military, but it’s about being able to close the gap between civil service and the military, to provide services to the people, protection of rights and freedoms, providing strategic health care and everything else that can provide opportunities for their economies to grow.”

a6471.speaker: General Michael Langley, Commander of the U.S. Africa Command (on the Gaborone conference)
a6471.speech: Described the Gaborone conference as the “Super Bowl or World Cup” of militaries meeting: “Coming together cannot be replaced by Zoom calls. We have to sit together in the same room and see the value of having engagements and sidebars in a continuous sense. We are looking at Africa-led, US-enabled solutions.”

a6587.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, UN spokesman
a6587.speech: "The Palestinian Authority is the authority we recognise across the whole Palestinian territory and we want the Palestinians to be able to choose their own future," he argued, also advocating the restoration of the ceasefire in Gaza to allow humanitarian aid ; "We want the release of the hostages," in addition to a "two-State solution", which is the UN's official position, he added.

a6587.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, UN spokesman
a6587.speech: During his daily press conference he also addressed the critical situation following the most recent Israeli attacks in Gaza: "It is clear that the humanitarian aid we need does not exist: there is not enough equipment, there is not enough fuel to operate the available equipment, and it is extremely difficult to try to find the people we hope have survived in these conditions," he lamented.

a6587.speaker: Mahmoud Abbas, President of the Palestinian Authority
a6587.speech: Made a claim regarding political control of the Gaza Strip and the need for the Palestinian Islamists of Hamas to lay down their weapons and release the 59 Israeli hostages still in their hands.

a6587.speaker: Local authorities in Gaza
a6587.speech: According to local authorities, the most recent Israeli attacks in Gaza have already caused 51,300 deaths.

a6587.speaker: Tel Aviv (Israeli authorities)
a6587.speech: According to Tel Aviv, Hamas's attack of 7 October caused about 1,200 deaths and 250 hostages.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On the origins of the project: said PEJACC "is the fruit of strategic reflection initiated by the Ministry of Agriculture" and responds to two major priorities, youth unemployment and the growing impacts of climate change, having been born out of a series of national consultations on sustainable development and building on the priorities established in the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On objectives, beneficiaries and funding: said PEJACC aims to strengthen horticultural and goat production systems to make them more resilient to climate impacts, promote inclusive and sustainable agribusiness and create decent jobs for young people and women, directly reaching nearly 80,000 people (about 12,000 households) with an indirect impact on 240,000 consumers in Djibouti City, in the regions of Ali Sabieh, Dikhil, Obock, Tadjourah, Arta and the peri-urban areas of Djibouti; said the project's overall amount of 57.4 million USD (10.4 billion Djibouti francs) is financed by a grant from the African Development Bank through several funds (ADF, TAF and the Climate Action Window) as well as a loan from IFAD, with a 10 million USD credit line to allow young people to start activities in the targeted value chains.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On the stakeholders: said PEJACC is by its very nature a cross-cutting project mobilising several sectors, with national stakeholders including the Ministries of Agriculture, Environment, Youth and of Women and the Family, WORLDVEG and the Institute of Life Sciences of the CERD for climate-smart technologies, the Djibouti Agency for Social Development (ADDS) for training of trainers and the incubation curriculum, and the Centre for Leadership and Entrepreneurship and the chamber of commerce for supporting SMEs; internationally the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) for the digital water-point monitoring system, the National Union of Djiboutian Women (UNFD) for gender-specific activities, the Djibouti Institute of Statistics (INSTAD) for updating the national livestock census, and youth associations and agricultural cooperatives.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On socio-economic benefits: said that in the short term the project will create 3,500 permanent and 2,300 temporary jobs, 60% for young people and 40% for women, with strengthened local capacities boosting food security; in the medium term a significant increase in horticultural production (tomato, aubergine, chilli, melon) and a 30% to 40% reduction in food dependence on imports; and in the long term a sustainable transformation of the horticultural and goat sectors with an increased contribution to national GDP and a positive environmental impact through better soil and water management.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On the primary sector's contribution to GDP: "Absolutely. PEJACC is designed to boost productivity and added value in the primary sector, by targeting precisely the horticultural and goat value chains." ; said that thanks to investments in infrastructure, access to credit (10 million USD) and the introduction of modern technologies the project will strengthen the competitiveness of farms, and that by supporting the creation of at least 200 small and medium-sized enterprises it will generate new economic opportunities, increasing the primary sector's contribution to GDP and fostering export prospects.

a6665.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Djiboutian Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources
a6665.speech: On climate readiness: said PEJACC is a structured and ambitious response to the challenges posed by climate change, which by integrating climate-smart practices and mobilising young people and women as drivers of change lays the foundations for sustainable adaptation, and that with a multisectoral approach and clear objectives the Republic of Djibouti is sending a strong signal that it is ready to transform climate challenges into opportunities for a prosperous and resilient future.

a6683.speaker: United Nations World Health Organisation (WHO) report released on Thursday
a6683.speech: Said that over 22,500 people — about a quarter of those injured in Gaza since Israel's recent offensive began — now face life-changing injuries that will require long-term rehabilitation, including severe limb damage, amputations, spinal cord trauma, traumatic brain injuries, and major burns; WHO's analysis, based on data from Emergency Medical Teams as of July 23, highlights the urgent need for both immediate and long-term rehabilitation support.

a6683.speaker: Dr. Richard Peeperkorn, WHO Representative in the occupied Palestinian territory
a6683.speech: Emphasised that the increasing demand for rehabilitation is occurring amid the near-total collapse of Gaza's healthcare infrastructure: "Patients are unable to receive the care they need. Acute rehabilitation services are critically disrupted, and specialised care for complex injuries is unavailable, jeopardising patients' lives. Immediate and ongoing support is urgently required to meet the massive rehabilitation needs."

a6683.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6683.speech: According to the WHO, only 17 out of Gaza's 36 hospitals are still partially operational, and primary healthcare and community services are frequently interrupted due to insecurity, attacks, and evacuation orders; the WHO reported that tens of thousands of Palestinians with chronic conditions or impairments are at greater risk due to the collapse of critical services.

a6683.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6683.speech: Stresses the need for safe access to essential health services, including rehabilitation, to mitigate further suffering, and continues to call for an immediate ceasefire to enable aid delivery, health system reconstruction, and life-saving interventions.

a6683.speaker: UNCTAD report published Thursday
a6683.speech: Said Gaza's economy has plummeted, with its gross domestic product (GDP) dropping by 81%, plunging the region into an unprecedented economic crisis, with massive job losses and rising unemployment exacerbating poverty; the report also notes severe disruptions to the economy of the West Bank due to violence, demolitions, confiscations, and settlement expansions, placing immense pressure on the Palestinian government's fiscal stability.

a6683.speaker: UNCTAD
a6683.speech: Urges the international community to intervene urgently to stabilize the economy, rebuild infrastructure, and support long-term peace efforts, including a comprehensive recovery plan for the occupied Palestinian territory, increased international aid, release of withheld revenues, and lifting the blockade on Gaza.

a6772.speaker: 2024 Yearbook on Media Quality in Tanzania, study by the School of Journalism and Mass Communication (SJMC) of the University of Dar es Salaam, funded by the Swiss Embassy and the British High Commission in Tanzania
a6772.speech: Revealed that radio stations across Tanzania performed poorly in promoting candidates' and citizens' voices in the November 27, 2024, local government elections; its findings show that out of 992 news and programmes reviewed from 35 radio stations across Tanzania, the most used source groups were political parties (37 per cent), followed by the executive government and its agencies (27 per cent), local government authorities (22 per cent), ordinary citizens (20 per cent) and party candidates (13 per cent): "The radio stations under review covered the candidates and their policies less than other issues. Yet, media coverage of candidates' policies allows citizens to make the right choices on election day."

a6772.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Commissioner General of the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
a6772.speech: Has stated that in ensuring a conducive and fair business environment, the authority is committed to combating tax evasion, and said that controlling tax evasion will create equal and favorable business conditions for those who comply with tax laws: "I want to take this opportunity to tell taxpayers who comply that we have been actively fighting tax evasion and taking various measures. Some deliberately evade taxes, and we have taken action against them. For example, over the past four years, we have prosecuted 77 taxpayers who attempted to evade taxes."

a6772.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Commissioner General of the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
a6772.speech: Urged Tanzanians and businesspeople not to engage in purchasing fake receipts to reduce their tax liability, warning that no one will escape detection, as tax violations will be uncovered; he further explained that TRA has been arresting individuals involved in counterfeiting electronic tax stamps, diverting goods meant for export (dumping), undervaluation, and misusing granted tax exemptions.

a6772.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Commissioner General of the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
a6772.speech: Stated that over the past four years, revenue collection has increased by 78 percent, a growth attributed to increased public awareness about tax payment and various government reforms aimed at improving TRA's operational efficiency.

a6772.speaker: Dr. Seif Shekalaghe, Permanent Secretary of Tanzania's Ministry of Health
a6772.speech: Issued a travel advisory on March 11, 2025, following the confirmation of the first Mpox cases in Tanzania, outlining measures to prevent the spread of the Mpox virus.

a6772.speaker: Tanzania Ministry of Health travel advisory (guidelines)
a6772.speech: "Travelers and border workers must observe hand hygiene, maintain at least a one-meter distance from others, and report any suspected symptoms by calling the toll-free number 199, notifying the border health office, or visiting the nearest health facility" ; "At border points, all travelers will undergo initial health screening, including body temperature checks, and those found with fever or rashes will undergo further medical examinations" ; "anyone who has been in contact with Mpox patients will be advised to monitor their health and report to the nearest health facility or call the toll-free number 199 if they develop symptoms of Mpox."

a6772.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6772.speech: Declared Mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in August 2024.

a6950.speaker: A local aid organisation in Jowhar (complaint)
a6950.speech: Has filed a complaint of extortion demands by Hirshabelle health officials in Jowhar, at a time when 3.5 million Somalis already face acute food insecurity and the number of severely malnourished children is also on the rise.

a6950.speaker: WARDI Relief Development Initiative
a6950.speech: Condemns and denies allegations published by some of the online Somali media referring its chairman to the alleged disappearance and death of Ikran Tahlil as well as some dispute resolution mechanism related to this matter.

a6950.speaker: South Sudanese government officials
a6950.speech: Claim that Internet blocking is not implemented in the country, despite yet another South Sudanese media site being blocked.

a6950.speaker: Documents seen by Horn Observer
a6950.speech: Show that under the presidency of Mohamed Abdullahi Farmajo the Somali government has employed fake journalists and social media campaigners to carry out a smear campaign against its political opponents and to troll journalists.

a6950.speaker: Report by the United Nations Secretary General released to the Security Council
a6950.speech: Says the security situation in Somalia remained volatile, with 1,086 attacks by the al-Qaeda-linked militants recorded in the past four months of the year.

a7094.speaker: Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) (statement)
a7094.speech: Announced that at least 38 people were injured, six of them seriously, in the emergency landing of a United Airlines plane in Lagos; said the Boeing 787-800 took off from Murtala Muhammed International Airport at 23:59 local time on Thursday bound for Washington, was forced to make an "emergency return" and landed "safely" at 03:22 local time on Friday with 245 adults and 11 crew members on board: "Four passengers and two crew members suffered serious injuries, and 27 passengers and five crew members suffered minor injuries," adding that "the aircraft itself did not suffer significant damage."

a7094.speaker: Leslie Scott, United Airlines spokeswoman
a7094.speech: Told CNN that six of the injured had already been discharged from hospital and that the reason for the plane's return was not severe turbulence, and that the airline is "working with US and Nigerian aviation authorities to understand the cause" of the incident.

a7094.speaker: Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA)
a7094.speech: Confirmed that it is investigating the case, which occurred over Ivory Coast's airspace.

a7094.speaker: Michael Achimugu, NCAA Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection (statement)
a7094.speech: "We are investigating the incident. We have received the flight data records in order to determine exactly what happened."

a7151.speaker: Chinese government data (General Administration of Customs)
a7151.speech: Showed that China's imports of Kuwaiti crude oil fell in May by 7.4 percent year-on-year to 318,000 barrels per day, and stated that China's imports of Kuwaiti oil exceeded 300,000 barrels per day for the third consecutive month; added that China's crude oil imports in the first five months of the year rose 5.6 percent over the same period of 2016 to 326,000 barrels per day, and that total Chinese crude imports rose 15.4 percent year-on-year in May to 8.8 million barrels per day, with Russia first (up 9.4 percent to 1.36 million bpd), Angola second (1.32 million bpd, up 79.2 percent), Saudi Arabia third (up 8.6 percent to one million bpd), and Oman and Iraq fourth and fifth.

a7287.speaker: Awahou Codjo Alabi, 2nd vice-president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a7287.speech: “This new situation, which is the logical continuation of the Single Window arrangement, makes it possible to manage the various stages from the sending of the ships' manifest through to departure from the port. It will take account of all the documents issued by the ministries concerned and other competent bodies in the form of authorizations or certificates.”

a7287.speaker: Awahou Codjo Alabi, 2nd vice-president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a7287.speech: According to the 2nd vice-president of the CCIB, this situation affects the performance of businesses and reduces their contribution to economic growth... the dematerialization of the ''pre-clearance bundles'' is a decisive step in the process of going fully digital in the handling of customs operations, she explained.

a7287.speaker: Awahou Codjo Alabi, 2nd vice-president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a7287.speech: The benefits of this tool will also translate into centralized invoicing and simple access to the regulations in force with daily updates, she welcomes ; This is a reform that benefits company heads, economic operators and Benin, insofar as it rests on technological advances and makes the country more competitive in terms of the speed of customs declaration operations, she praised. According to her, the project is part of the continuation of the reforms undertaken by Benin to improve the business environment.

a7287.speaker: Doing Business 2015 report
a7287.speech: According to the Doing Business 2015 report, 56% of import time and 64% of export time is devoted to pre-clearance formalities. The same source indicates that the processing times for customs clearance documents represented on average fifteen days out of the twenty-five for imports of the overall goods-processing time.

a7287.speaker: Florian Legroux, project manager for Benin's new single window for foreign trade
a7287.speech: Explained that the aim is to facilitate trade with the outside world by simplifying pre-clearance procedures and reducing document preparation times for both imports and transit exports. It will also have an impact on the direct and indirect costs associated with these procedures.

a7287.speaker: Florian Legroux, project manager for Benin's new single window for foreign trade
a7287.speech: Explained that in terms of the stakes it will make it possible, among other things, to strengthen the administration's operational effectiveness and to bring together the information needed to take the best decisions regarding foreign trade. It will involve, he continued, setting up a public portal of secure information that will network foreign-trade economic operators and that will inform them about the texts of laws, the procedures and the documents relating to cross-border trade. All of this consultable online.
